# requireValidSlug

<link-summary>Returns the value as a slug, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireValidSlug() — Returns the value as a slug, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/string</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireValidSlug(
  value: string | null | undefined,
  message: string = "Expected a valid slug."
): string;
```

Starts with a letter, then letters, digits, hyphens and underscores — the shape a URL segment or a key can take. Spaces, leading digits and an empty string are rejected.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                           | Type                          | Description                                                   |
| :-------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                             | `string \| null \| undefined` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a valid slug."` | `string`                      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`string` — the same value, typed as a slug.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                |
| :------------------------- | :----------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a slug. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireValidSlug("my-page"); // => "my-page"
requireValidSlug("a_1"); // => "a_1"
requireValidSlug("1-page"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireValidSlug("my page"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
